videos.title: Perplexity just reinvented the computer with computer.
videos.creator: Roberto Nickson (RPN)
videos.transcript:
Perplexity just reinvented the computer with computer.
And it's time to pay attention because it's going to be hard to compete with somebody using this.
Why?
What is it?
Well, think of it like Open Claude with an easier setup and without the security nightmare.
How does it do this?
Well, when you describe a desired outcome, let's say, pull live financials on Apple, Microsoft, and Google, build me an interactive comparison dashboard with charts, and create a 30-second narrated video breaking down which stock is a stronger buy.
Computer breaks this down into tasks and subtasks and creates and coordinates multiple agents for the best results.
It's like your personal team of senior level employees.
For example, it might use Opus 4.6 for core reasoning, Gemini 3.1 for the deep market research and GPT-5.4 to cross-reference the financial data.
Once that's complete, it'll deploy the live dashboard using Sonnet 4.6, generate the charts with Nano Banana 2, and produce the narrated video with VO 3.1.
Now you start to see the power of multi-model orchestration because there is no one-size-fits-all model.
I mean, each has their own specialization.
Perplexity computer is the missing piece to get all the best models to work together.
And it's not just finance.
I mean, I asked what specific steps I could take to become the best possible creator in tech to research my top 10 competitors, build a battle card for each one, and then package the whole thing into a slide deck.
I mean, take a look, right?
What used to take my team a full week was done before my coffee got cold.
Then you add the hundreds of connectors available like Gmail, Slack, Google Calendar, GitHub, Linear, Hubspot to give it the full context of your work.
You start to understand why this is such an unfair advantage, especially in these early days where multi-agent AI adoption is remarkably low.
Computer, it's the perfect name.
It's the first time I feel like I can leverage the power of my PC with a single interface.
So comment computer, and I'll send you a link to try it.
videos.caption:
Perplexity just reinvented the computer, with Computer.

Think of it like OpenClaw without the security vulnerabilities. To me this is the closest thing we have to Jarvis for the average consumer. 

The magic of Computer is the multi-model orchestration. Meaning, when you give it a high-level task, this beast breaks it down into multiple sub-tasks to run in parallel, tapping into 19+ frontier models to automatically assign the right one to each sub-task.

Combined with thousands of app connections, @perplexity Computer is capable of end-to-end execution across the entire context of your work.

Comment “Computer” and I’ll send you a link to try it.

videos.title: Meta just launched some of the most revolutionary consumer tech products of the year.
videos.creator: Roberto Nickson (RPN)
videos.transcript:
Meta just launched some of the most revolutionary consumer tech products of the year.
Meta Ray-Ban Display and Meta Neural Band, which will fundamentally change the way you interact with the world.
Let me show you why.
So, we're all familiar with Ray-Ban Meta.
Meta Ray-Ban Display features a full-color monocular display built right into the lens, which is super useful because you can see your notifications, messages, video calls, live translation, AI information, and navigation overlays without having to take out your phone.
You can also capture hands-free POV footage with an ultra-wide 12-megapixel camera with viewfinder and 3x zoom functionality and preview your photos in display before capturing.
Now, to interact with the glasses, you can use the four-way capacitive touchpad which you may be familiar with, or, and this is the crazy part because it feels like magic, you can use Meta Neural Band.
Look, every new computing platform comes with a new way to interact.
The Meta Neural Band uses industry-leading EMG technology, which basically interprets electrical signals created by your muscle activity to control the glasses.
It is a huge technical feat because everybody's muscles are different, so breakthrough deep learning algorithms were developed so it works out of the box for nearly anyone.
I can guarantee that the first time you try it to silently scroll and click, you'll be amazed.
Now, all the details and specifics are in the caption, but to me, this is a very exciting breakthrough in wearable tech.
Let me know if you plan on copping, and I'll see you next time.
videos.caption:
The day is finally here. #MetaRayBan Display is officially available.

Experience the first AI glasses with a private in-lens display and on-wrist control with Meta Neural Band.

Book a hands-on demo at Meta Lab or Best Buy.

- 600x600 full-color, vivid monocular display (first of its kind)
- Quickly and privately respond to messages... spend less time pulling out your phone.
- Live captions and translations

And more.

Who’s picking one up?

videos.title: Apple just dropped the iPhone 16 with something we didn't expect.
videos.creator: Roberto Nickson (RPN)
videos.transcript:
Apple just dropped the iPhone 16 with something we didn't expect.
But before you order, let's take a look.
Yeah, it's a little bigger, faster, the screen's a little stronger, all that's expected.
But let's focus on the big thing here.
These devices are now built with Apple Intelligence at the center.
Let's start with Siri.
It now has a rich deep understanding of all your personal context.
As an example, you can say, "Hey, send Erica all the pictures from last week's barbecue." And it has on screen awareness, so if a friend text you a song, you can just say, "Play that." Now, you can access Apple Intelligence from the iPhone 15 Pro, but the iPhone 16 has something unique to it.
It's called Visual Intelligence, meaning you can point your camera to what you're seeing and ask questions about it, like, "Hey, what kind of dog is this?" or, "This bike looks pretty cool, where can I buy it?" So, if that's important to you, upgrade.
If not, I don't think it's worth it.
Unless you rely on your iPhone camera for work, because it's incredibly impressive, especially on the Pro models.
There's a new 48-megapixel Fusion camera and a 48-megapixel ultra-wide camera that enables macro photography, which is really damn cool.
And we have a new button for camera controls with a wide variety of gestures, but my favorite part about the camera, we now have 4k 120 FPS video.
Crazy.
And an audio mix feature, which uses machine learning to isolate the audio you want from any background noise.
I'm definitely picking the 16 Pro up and it's going to replace my cinema camera for a lot of the stuff that I do.
So, my opinion, if you use the camera professionally or for work, get a Pro model.
If you're looking to save time and hassle with Apple Intelligence, upgrade to the non-pro model.
Otherwise, you're probably okay with the device you already have.
Let me know what you think.
Peace.
videos.caption:
Apple has officially announced the iPhone 16 lineup… but should you pick one up? Here’s what to know before you order.

#apple #iphone #iphone16

videos.caption:

pair this with a voice call that matches your voice and sounds perfectly realistic, it might not be so hard to convince her to wire money.

videos.title: Let me show you the craziest part about the Vision Pro.
videos.creator: Roberto Nickson (RPN)
videos.transcript:
Let me show you the craziest part about the Vision Pro.
I am now convinced that we've entered a transition into a screenless world.
So this is my spatial computing setup, and I can get my work done in a two-monitor setup.
I can get in close to the details, I'm facetiming with my beautiful wife, I have my Instagram feed to the side, I got a YouTube video playing on top, shout out to Casey, Twitter, news, I can customize this however I want.
That's not the crazy part.
The crazy part is that because of spatial awareness, and Carly, you're coming with me, I can actually leave apps running wherever I want in the environment.
So I walk to our refrigerator, we have a grocery list there.
We'll be traveling soon, so I leave a packing list in the kitchen.
I can have sports running or maybe I want to watch a movie or show, I need to finish Killers of the Flower Moon.
See, customization is limitless here and your surroundings become an infinite canvas.
So, let me grab Carly.
Let me go pay her a visit, because when you Facetime somebody from the Vision Pro, this is what you look like.
Definitely dystopian.
Now, as I said before, the Vision Pro, this is the most incredible consumer tech product that I've ever tried, without a doubt.
But, unless you're a developer, or if 3,500 bucks is just play money to you, I can't recommend you buy it.
Honestly, I think the Quest 3 is like 82% of the way here at 1/7th of the price.
Maybe best to wait for a version two, three, four.
But let me know what you think below.
Catch you in the next one.
Peace.
videos.caption:
Are we entering into a decades-long transition into a world of screen-less computing? I can finally see it. The Vision Pro is the device that dramatically accelerates a move into that direction.

The confluence of spatial computing, AI, improved hardware and battery technology could result in a highly ergonomic device that will replace our screens.

The Vision and Quest platforms will continue to improve their form factors and ergonomics.

After 72 hours with the Vision Pro, I will reiterate that it is the most incredible consumer tech device I’ve ever tried. But aside from some very specific cases, I can’t recommend it as a buy. My advice would be to wait for a version 2 or 3. The Meta Quest 3 can do 85% of what the Vision Pro can do at 1/7th the price with a much more mature app and games ecosystem.

I also want to mention that the theater experience in the Vision Pro is remarkable. I think the combination of the Vision Pro + AirPods Max can already replace a $10,000 home theater system. The only caveat is that it’s single player.  What are your thoughts on the Vision Pro?  #visionpro #applevisionpro #tech
